idiom_name: importlib.metadata entry points (plus pkgutil namespace discovery)
implementation_notes: Packaged plugins announce themselves in distribution metadata: a project declares an entry point group in pyproject.toml, and the host lists it with entry_points(group="myapp.plugins") and never imports anything until EntryPoint.load() is called - metadata-only discovery is exactly the read-the-descriptor-first step. What replaces the classic structure is a dict registry built from entry-point names plus the import system; for plugins that are not installed distributions, the accepted alternatives are a namespace package scanned with pkgutil.iter_modules(ns_pkg.__path__) followed by importlib.import_module, or a naming convention such as flask_*. importlib.metadata supersedes the older pkg_resources entry-point API, and the classic structure is only worth rebuilding behind a process boundary when plugins need isolation or independent dependency versions.
pitfalls: Entry points come from installed distribution metadata, so a plugin dropped into a directory is invisible until it is installed (or a path-inspecting loader is written); stale dist-info caches survive uninstalls.
Calling .load() at discovery time imports plugin modules and runs their top-level code - the common way a broken plugin breaks host start-up; resolve lazily and catch exceptions per plugin.
Two plugins using the same entry-point name silently shadow each other in a dict, and a plugin that turns the host's package into a namespace package can break the host's own imports.
